note: Holdings-relevant market news, researched daily by the intel agent (multi-theme sweep: precious metals, HK tech, SGX/Singapore, rare earths, macro) with sources. The "actionable" line relates each item to this specific portfolio. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Silver slips back below $60 (~$60.4/oz), ends the week down ~4% as firmer oil and US-Iran tension revive higher-for-longer Fed bets
items.summary: Silver traded around $60.43/oz on Friday 11 July after slipping under $60 intraweek, ending the week down about 4% — a sharp reversal of the prior week's ~6% rebound. The move tracked rising crude and renewed US-Iran hostilities that pushed rate-hike-repricing back to the fore, lifting the 10-year toward 4.57% and the dollar. The structural deficit thesis is intact (Silver Institute 46.3Moz 2026 deficit; JPMorgan ~$81 average), but volatility remains brutal after January's ~$120 peak halved in June.
items.actionable: The levered-silver stack gave back last week's bounce — higher-for-longer rates and a firm dollar are the live threat, not the deficit story. Keep leverage sized so a break of ~$58 can't force liquidation into the 14 July CPI, which is now the binary that decides the next leg.

items.headline: June US CPI lands 14 July: headline may print negative (~-0.1% m/m, ~3.9% y/y) on the oil plunge, but core seen sticky at +0.3%/~2.9%
items.summary: The BLS releases June CPI on 14 July at 8:30am ET. June's mid-month ceasefire and Hormuz reopening dropped oil ~21% intra-month, so headline CPI could flip slightly negative (consensus ~-0.1% m/m, ~3.9% y/y), but the Fed-relevant core is expected to grind +0.3% (~2.9% y/y). CME FedWatch shows ~75% odds of a 28-29 July hold and ~25% for a 25bp hike, with the Warsh Fed's dots pencilling a possible 2026 hike (median ~3.8% end-2026). A hot core would revive the hike repricing that crushed metals in June.
items.actionable: This is THE event risk of the week for the levered silver/gold stack. A soft core buys metals room; a hot core (>0.3%) re-arms the September-hike tail. Keep option/stop protection on through the print and treat the big cash pile as optionality, not a drag.

items.headline: Hong Kong tech rips: Hang Seng +3%, HSTECH +5% as Alibaba +12%, Xiaomi +9%, SMIC +7.5% on eased lock-up fears and AI momentum
items.summary: Hong Kong stocks surged on Wednesday 8 July, the Hang Seng closing +3% and the Hang Seng Tech Index +5% to ~4,731. Alibaba jumped >12% on faster-than-expected loss-narrowing at Taobao Quick Commerce, Xiaomi +9%, SMIC +7.5% as mainland investors chased China-AI 'picks-and-shovels', and Tencent and Lenovo also rallied. A feared wave of post-IPO lock-up expiries was absorbed without a sell-off, easing a key overhang.
items.actionable: A clean tailwind for the HK tech sleeve (Tencent, SMIC, Xiaomi) — the lock-up overhang clearing plus the domestic-AI bid supports holding. Size for volatility: these names swing 7-12% in a session, so add on pullbacks rather than chasing the spike.

items.headline: Straits Times Index hits a fresh record ~5,469 (+0.65% Fri); DBS/OCBC/UOB crushed the STI in 1H26 (+19-28%)
items.summary: The STI rose 35.41 points (+0.65%) to a record 5,469.29 on Friday 10 July on broad-based buying, up further from ~5,244 the prior week. First-half 2026 total returns confirmed bank leadership: OCBC +28.2%, DBS +19.3%, UOB +15%, versus +13.1% for the SPDR STI ETF. Banks and REITs dominate the Q2 SGX earnings calendar now beginning.
items.actionable: The SGX sleeve (DBS, Singtel, REITs, developers) is riding a record index, but with the banks up 15-28% into results, favor adding S-REITs (which benefit from a lower SORA) over paying up for banks near ~2.2x book. DBS reports ~6 August.

items.headline: Tencent's near-daily buyback continues — 1.1m shares for HK$500.7m on 9 July after a lighter 8 July tranche
items.summary: HKEX filings show Tencent repurchased ~1.1m shares for HK$500.7m on 9 July and a smaller 27,600 shares for HK$12.7m on 8 July, extending the relentless daily cadence (HK$500m tranches on 2, 3, 9 July). The buyback runs under the ~912m-share (10%) mandate from the 13 May 2026 AGM, mechanically shrinking the count while the stock trades around HK$450-470.
items.actionable: Hold 0700.HK; the persistent HK$500m/day buyback bid offers downside support and compounds per-share value — consider adding on dips toward HK$450 rather than chasing after the 8 July tech spike.

items.headline: Oil books a ~4% weekly gain (Brent ~$75.5, WTI ~$71) as Trump calls the Iran ceasefire 'over' and Hormuz shipping stays disrupted
items.summary: Crude jumped after President Trump said the US-Iran ceasefire was effectively over following renewed military exchanges, though both sides agreed to keep technical/peace talks open. Brent settled around $75.5 and WTI ~$71 on Friday 10 July, each up ~3.5-4.7% on the week, as disruption to the Strait of Hormuz (~20% of world oil/gas trade) kept a risk premium bid. Firmer oil is inflationary at the margin ahead of the CPI print.
items.actionable: The returning war premium is a two-way risk: near-term supportive for the metals safe-haven bid, but firmer oil feeds the hawkish-Fed narrative that crushed silver in June. Don't add to levered silver on a geopolitical spike — those bids faded fast last month.

items.headline: Gold consolidates near $4,050-4,075 as a firm dollar and higher-for-longer Fed cap upside; PBoC keeps buying
items.summary: Gold traded around $4,050-4,076/oz into 8 July, firm but rangebound after June's ~11% slide, as a resilient dollar (DXY firm) and the fading of 2026 rate-cut hopes offset a steady central-bank bid. Goldman holds a ~$4,900 year-end target while JPMorgan stays more bullish (~$6,000 by Q4); the PBoC's continued official gold accumulation provides a demand floor under the price.
items.actionable: Gold's central-bank floor cushions the GDX/miner sleeve, but a hawkish Fed and firm dollar cap it — treat ~$4,000 as the line that matters for the miners, and don't expect gold to rescue silver on its own into the CPI print.

items.headline: 10-year Treasury yield backs up to ~4.57% (highest since 22 May), up ~9bp on the week, on firmer oil and hawkish repricing
items.summary: The 10-year yield rose about 9bp on the week to ~4.568% — up 8 of the last 9 sessions and the highest since 22 May — as firmer oil and a hawkish, higher-for-longer Warsh Fed pushed rates up. The dollar index ended the week higher. Money-market funds pulled in a large +$56.4B while investment-grade credit saw its biggest inflow since June 2020 (+$16.7B), and Treasuries logged their largest outflow in 9 weeks (-$2.7B).
items.actionable: Rising real rates and a firm dollar are the direct headwind for the levered-metals book. The big cash pile is earning ~3.6-3.75% risk-free — keep it as dry powder; any long-duration (TLT) adds should wait for a hawkish-surprise backup rather than chasing here.

items.headline: China blacklists MP Materials & USA Rare Earth (export-control list); G7 moves to cap Chinese rare-earth imports at 60%
items.summary: China's MOFCOM added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to an export-control list on 22 June, days after the G7 agreed to cap Chinese rare-earth imports at 60%, and formalized enforcement (a tip-reward mechanism live 1 July) covering samarium, gadolinium and lutetium compounds. MP fell ~13.4% in June on the listing even though it doesn't sell to China; it and Lynas anchor ex-China supply (~15% of global NdPr by 2026) under Western-government backing (MP's 10-year DoD price floor).
items.actionable: Tighter Chinese enforcement plus the G7 cap raise the scarcity premium on ex-China supply and validate the onshoring thesis — treat MP/LYC.AX/UUUU pullbacks (MP still ~off its highs) on the watchlist as scale-in candidates funded from cash, while 6680.HK (JL MAG) carries the export-cap headwind.

items.headline: SK Hynix raises $26.5B in the largest-ever US listing by a foreign company; ADRs pop 12.8% on AI-memory demand
items.summary: SK Hynix American depositary receipts jumped 12.8% above their offering price after the Korean memory maker raised $26.5B in the biggest-ever US listing by a foreign company, capping a winning week for semiconductors. Nvidia rose ~4% and Meta ~15% on the week (its best since early 2024), reasserting the AI-bottleneck leadership that had wobbled on 7 July.
items.actionable: The AI/memory demand signal supports the semiconductor-localization sleeve (SMH as the deploy vehicle, 0981.HK SMIC on the southbound side) — but Burry's fresh chip shorts are the counter-risk, so phase in on strength rather than going all-in near record levels.

items.headline: Bitcoin holds ~$64k (+2.8% on the week) as ETF inflows and CLARITY Act optimism offset Middle East risk
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $64,000 into 10-11 July, up ~2.8% over seven days with ETH ~$1,795 (+2.7%), as ETF inflows and rising optimism over the pending CLARITY Act crypto-market-structure bill supported prices even through renewed Middle East conflict — a show of relative resilience. BTC remains well off early-2026 highs after the hawkish Fed removed 2026 rate-cut hopes.
items.actionable: Bitcoin's steadiness is a useful risk-appetite gauge for the book — its resilience despite the hawkish rates backdrop is a mild positive tell, but keep any crypto sizing small; a dovish Fed pivot or CLARITY passage is the needed upside catalyst.

items.headline: Fund flows flash defensive: US growth -$5.0B (worst since March), mid-cap -$5.7B; cash +$56.4B, IG credit +$16.7B (best since 2020)
items.summary: BofA's Flow Show (EPFR data, week to 2 July) showed a defensive rotation: money-market funds +$56.4B and investment-grade credit +$16.7B (biggest since June 2020), against US growth-fund outflows of -$5.0B (worst since March) and US mid-cap -$5.7B (worst since July 2023). US equities saw a second straight weekly outflow (-$1.9B) and Japan a fourth (-$2.8B); only Europe kept drawing inflows (+$0.6B). Gold +$1.4B and crypto +$1B stayed positive.
items.actionable: Smart money is de-risking crowded US growth into cash and quality credit, not selling everything — consistent with holding the big cash pile and favoring quality/defensive over chasing narrow tech. Gold-fund inflows corroborate keeping the metals sleeve.

items.headline: Lynas ramps toward 10-12ktpa NdPr as ex-China separators re-rate; Energy Fuels builds heavy-REE circuit with $725M US backing
items.summary: Lynas, the largest non-Chinese separator (~7ktpa NdPr-equivalent), is pushing toward ~10-12ktpa capacity and expects higher rare-earth prices after US backing of MP Materials, amid a CEO transition (Lacaze out 1 July, Le Roux interim). Energy Fuels is modifying its White Mesa circuits from July to add heavy rare earths (Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy) alongside NdPr, backed by a conditional $725M US Office of Strategic Capital financing tied to acquiring Australian Strategic Materials.
items.actionable: Washington keeps putting a financing/price floor under Western rare-earth economics — watchlist scale-in candidates on pullbacks (REMX for the basket, MP/LYC.AX/UUUU for single names), but note Lynas's CEO transition and UUUU's ASM integration/dilution overhang argue for letting them settle rather than chasing.
